agree.reason: The plain apology, the weekly email and the credit when weather cuts a box by more than a third deal directly with this household's complaints that the farm went quiet and kept their money, so they will probably reconsider, though nothing is offered for last year's losses.

honest.reason: Every commitment and figure comes from the facts given, but 'many of you' blurs 29 of 41 respondents, and 'half what it should have' drops the 'about' from 'about half'.

works_the_facts.reason: The email repeats the raw facts and works out nothing from them: it doesn't use 29 of 41, it doesn't give the weekly value of a share (about $24.50), and it doesn't show the credit last year's six thin weeks would have earned under the new policy.

right_comparison.reason: The only comparison is that the price hasn't changed; the email never sets last year's handling (no credit, one email) against what the same storm would mean this year, beyond listing the changes.

qualification.reason: The hedge is specific and the reader can check it: no promise of zero loss, the greens are not netted, and any box cut by more than a third gets a credit; it lacks an amount or timing for the credit.

objections.reason: The objection that the farm went silent and kept their money is answered head-on by the apology, the weekly email and the credit, and the email raises no objection the facts already settle.

fit.reason: It is a short email of about 190 words with a subject line, a link, the deadline and a signature, as the brief asked.
